target_customer: Grocery and retail chains with existing cameras, loss prevention and store operations teams
problem: Retailers lose money to missed scans and theft and cannot afford to replace cameras at $50K to $100K per site. Lexius adds AI to existing cameras and matches video to the register log.
business_model: B2B software per store; pricing not public, free trials in stores reported
product_category: Computer vision for retail loss prevention

founders.name: David Elskamp
education: BA and MA in Computer Science (schools not named on the YC page)
previous_startups: A media company started at 14, run for 8 years, six figure revenue (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a two time founder.

competitors.name: Everseen
competitors.what: Vision AI for checkout loss detection including missed scans

technical_complexity.rationale: AI must work on low quality, fragmented legacy CCTV and reach accuracy high enough for loss decisions, as the YC page says.

defensibility.rationale: POS integrations and video data from many stores help, but Everseen and other vendors sell similar detection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Scandit announced a competing product in 2026; no acquisition of Lexius found.

market_need_then: The ECR 2026 self checkout loss report found missed scans in roughly 1% to 4.8% of transactions; Lexius shows logos such as Erewhon and Pak'nSave on its site and a Marino's Market case study.

branding.domain_note: Uses lexius.ai; no purchase details found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Retail and operations focused; tagline Every basket. Accounted for.

brand_strength.rationale: A coined legal sounding name with no found press about the brand; the YC profile and trade coverage (IPVM) focus on the product.

pivots.from: General AI security guard for corporate cameras (shoplifting, slip and falls)
pivots.to: Checkout missed scan detection at staffed lanes and self checkout
pivots.why: A 2026 article says focus narrowed to missed scans; the website now leads with checkout. The exact date is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Lexius is a Winter 2026 company, active, with retail logos and a narrowed checkout wedge. No outcome yet. Competition from Everseen and Scandit and the hard messy CCTV problem are the main risks, while store trials show early pull.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists a $0.5M convertible note dated 2026-01-01 with YC, and Caplight lists $1M total and a 2026-02-26 accelerator round; both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. An IPVM headline about a shut down camera startup is not tied to Lexius. The pivot date is approximate and the pivot is inferred from the YC page versus the later site and article.
